Chapter 8
Integrating with Embedded Extended
Warehouse Management
Embedded extended warehouse management in SAP S/4HANA makes it
far more efficient and effective for companies to perform quality func-
tions in logistics and the supply chain that involve complex warehousing
functions.
Warehousing operations are closely linked with the sales, procurement, production,
and distribution (inbound and outbound) processes in the supply chain, as well as with
financial accounting. Good warehousing management should both support the
smooth flow of materials to and from the warehouse and provide useful information
to run the operations within the warehouse.
Embedded extended warehouse management (EWM) in SAP S/4HANA has led to the
following massive simplifications:
 Direct access to master data and configuration objects
 Elimination of the core interface (CIF) for transferring master data
 Reduction of redundant transaction objects in embedded EWM and SAP S/4HANA
Note
The queued remote function call (qRFC) is still required to transfer transaction data
from and to SAP S/4HANA and embedded EWM (see Figure 8.1). Engage an SAP Net-
Weaver consultant to ensure the required qRFC setup is up and running.
The chapter begins by explaining the minimal configuration required to integrate QM
with embedded EWM, followed by discussing the relevant master data setup. Next, we
provide an end-to end walkthrough of the integrated business processes. The chapter
concludes with reporting, including the warehouse management monitor.
Note
In this chapter, we’ll describe the functionality of embedded EWM in sufficient detail
for the purposes of its integration with QM; however, we won’t cover every possible
business scenario. We’ll restrict the scope of this chapter to typical and routine busi-
ness processes that use materials management (MM), QM, and the embedded EWM

8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management

areas only. Due to the highly integrated nature of QM with other areas, it’s always best
to coordinate with experts or consultants in these SAP areas to ensure you’re meeting
the end-to-end business scenarios of a client where SAP S/4HANA (with embedded
EWM) is being implemented.

The following sections begin with covering only the configuration elements in embed-
ded EWM that have a direct bearing on the QM processes.
8.1 Configuration Basics
Objects created or configured in an SAP area are then assigned to master data, which is
covered in the next section of this chapter. Standard solutions and configurations
delivered by embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA are sufficient to independently config-
ure, implement, and integrate QM with embedded EWM.
Table 8.1 consists of various inspection types available in SAP S/4HANA that find
greater usage in embedded EWM areas and into which you can integrate the QM area.
Ensure that you assign and activate the relevant inspection types in the material mas-
ter. Refer to Chapter 2, wherein the configuration details of an inspection type are dis-
cussed in detail.

8.1 Configuration Basics
The following sections discuss the QM-specific configurations that need to be in place
so that the configured objects are then assigned to the master data.
8.1.1 Activate Inspection Object Type
An inspection object type defines the following:
 Business process for the inspection
 Inspected object—for example, the product, the handling unit, or the delivery
 Warehouse number
Each inspection object type can have many inspection rules. Based on selection criteria
(also known as properties), the inspection rule determines which objects to trigger an
inspection for and specifies the inspection details—for example, the inspection pro-
cess, the procedure, the inspection frequency, and usage decision codes, as well as their
associated logistical functions.
There are six inspection object types to cater to different business processes, as shown
in Table 8.2.
Inspection Type Inspection Plan Usage Inspection Type Description
17 9 Extended Warehouse Inspection (EWM)
1701 9 EWM: Goods receipt inspection for pur-
chase order
1704 9 EWM: Goods receipt inspection from
production
1708 9 EWM: Stock transfer inspection
1709 9 EWM: Recurring inspection of batches
Table 8.1 Inspection Types in Embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA
Inspection Object Type Description
1 Preliminary inspection – inbound delivery
2 Counting inbound deliveries
3 Quality inspection – return delivery
4 Quality inspection for product/batch – inbound delivery
5 Quality inspection for product/batch warehouse – internal
6 Preliminary inspection – handling unit
Table 8.2 Inspection Object Types

8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management
366
Note
Inspection object types 1 to 3 are still not available in embedded EWM with the SAP
S/4HANA 2023 release but are expected to be available in future releases.
When integrating with QM, you can define that the inspection setup data of the Quality
Management view in the material master is used. An inspection rule is no longer
required. In embedded EWM, the inspection types 01 (goods receipt inspection for pur-
chase order), 04 (goods receipt inspection from production), 08 (stock transfer inspec-
tion), and 09 (recurring inspection of batches) are supported. For sampling, the
following is true:
 When using the business process acceptance sampling, you specify the inspection
type in the quality info record for the material.
 When using the business process presampling in production, you specify the inspec-
tion type in the Quality Management view of the material master.
Note
If you want to change your settings from inspections with inspection rules to inspec-
tions without inspection rules, refer to SAP Note 2787302.
You can use quality inspection without inspection rules in the following processes:
 Acceptance sampling
 Inspections after goods receipt
 Presampling in production
 Stock inspections
 Recurring inspections
To configure and define quality inspection without inspection rules, follow menu path
SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Manage-
ment  Cross-Process Settings  Quality Management  Basics and Integration  Define
and Activate Warehouse-Dependent Activation of IOTs (Inspection Object Types). Here,
you’ll find the following:
 For Inspection Setup Origin, you specify that no inspection rule is used and that the
inspection lot setup originates from the Quality Management tab of the material
master.
 Under Insp. Planning without Rules, you specify the inspection settings and the
quality inspection process.

8.1 Configuration Basics
Let’s now discuss how to set up QM integration with embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA.
You need to activate an inspection object type for a warehouse so it can be used. To do
so, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended
Warehouse Management  Cross-Process Settings  Quality Management  Basics and
Integration  Define and Activate Warehouse-Dependent Activation of IOTs.
The screen that appears, as shown in Figure 8.2, shows the control functions that can be
applied for the quality inspection process in embedded EWM. The last two options con-
trol if the system should look for inspection rule setup in embedded EWM for quality
inspection processes or in the material master of SAP S/4HANA. Figure 8.3 shows the
options available for inspection planning without the rules.
Figure 8.2 Inspection Object Type

Figure 8.3 Inspection Planning without Rules
8.1.2 Maintain Inspection Object Types Version
Maintaining an inspection object type version in embedded EWM is one of the prereq-
uisites for quality inspection processing. To maintain an inspection object type ver-
sion, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended
Warehouse Management  Cross-Process Settings  Quality Management  Basics and
Integration  Maintain Inspection Object Types Version.
In Figure 8.4, select the checkboxes under the Activ. IOT (active inspection object) col-
umn for relevant business processes. For example, inspection object type 4 will trigger
quality inspection for incoming or inbound materials (goods receipt), whereas inspec-
tion object type 5 will trigger quality inspection when one stock type moves to another
(e.g., from unrestricted or blocked stock to quality stock).
Figure 8.4 Inspection Type Object Version
Figure 8.5 shows the detailed level of properties for inspection object type 4 and is a
control function on the level of details an inspection rule needs to have. For example,
if a country of origin doesn’t influence the quality inspection process in any way, then
this field can be removed from the list so that it won’t appear while creating an inspec-
tion rule for the material (or the warehouse product) in the warehouse.

8.1.3 Define and Assign Follow-Up Actions
You can maintain follow-up actions for an inspection outcome—that is, while recoding
the usage decision of an inspection lot. Follow-up actions are used for quality control or
simply for informative purposes. To define follow-up actions, use menu path SAP IMG 
SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Management  Cross
Process Settings  Quality Management  Inspection Results  Maintain Follow-Up
Actions  Define Follow-up Actions.
Figure 8.6 shows the control functions of follow-up actions that can be applied to an
inspection lot or to a usage decision by choosing the relevant option from the drop-
down available under the FolUpAct column.
Select the EWM_A follow-up function, and then choose Function Modules from the left
side of the screen so that the screen in Figure 8.7 appears.
Figure 8.6 Follow-Up Actions for Inspection Results

8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management
370
Figure 8.7 Details of Follow-Up Actions
Figure 8.7 shows the standard function module that will trigger the embedded EWM
logistical follow-up action we cover next. An existing or standard function module can
be changed or a new one created and assigned to a usage decision to meet any specific
business need. It’s best to engage an ABAP consultant for this task.
Once the follow-up actions are defined, the next step is to assign embedded EWM logis-
tical actions to the previously defined follow-up function. To do so, follow menu path
SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Management 
Cross Process Settings  Quality Management  Inspection Results  Maintain Follow-
Up Actions  Assign Logistical Follow-Up Actions.
Figure 8.8 shows the detailed screen with entries for the previously defined FolUpAct
“EWM_A” with IOT “4” for Warehouse No. “1710”. In Assign Logistical Follow-Up
Actions, it’s possible to control how and where the stock moves when it’s assigned a
specific follow-up logistical action.

8.1 Configuration Basics
8.1.4 Quality Inspection Group
The quality inspection group identifies products that behave or are handled in the same
way during quality inspection processing. To simplify the maintenance of inspection
rules in embedded EWM, you can assign quality inspection groups to the relevant
products. You can also use these groups in the inspection rule maintenance instead of
the product number (or warehouse product).
It’s important to note here that because EWM is now embedded in SAP S/4HANA, each
material master created in SAP S/4HANA also automatically creates a warehouse prod-
uct in which detailed information about warehouse management and processing can
be maintained.
Access the screen in Figure 8.9 via Transaction /SAPAPO/MAT1, and on the initial
screen that appears, enter material master “RM124” in the Product field (referred to as a
product in embedded EWM). In the Storage tab, assign Q-Insp. Grp as “0001” as shown.
Figure 8.9 Warehouse Product
Note
To define a quality inspection group so you can assign it in the screen in Figure 8.9, fol-
low menu path SAP IMG  Integration with Other SAP Components  Definition 
Extended Warehouse Management  Additional Material Attributes  Attribute Values
for Additional Material Master Fields  Define Quality Inspection Group.

8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management
372
8.1.5 Define and Assign Work Centers
Just as it was required to create a quality work center in SAP S/4HANA for quality
inspection processing, a similar work center creation is required in embedded EWM. To
do so, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended
Warehouse Management  Master Data  Work Center  Define Work Center.
Figure 8.10 shows Work Center YQIC created for Warehouse No. 1010. Because most set-
tings on this screen directly control warehouse management processing in embedded
EWM, it’s best to coordinate with the EWM consultant to make the necessary settings
here.
Figure 8.10 Inspection Work Center
The embedded EWM quality work center created in the previous step is assigned to a
warehouse as a default value so that that the system is able to assign it automatically
during inspection processing. To assign a default work center for inspection, follow
menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse
Management  Cross-Process Settings  Quality Management  Result  Assign Default
Work Center for Inspections.
Figure 8.11 shows that work center YQIC is assigned to warehouse number 1010.

8.2 Master Data Setup
Figure 8.11 Default Inspection Work Center Warehouse
This brings an end to the embedded EWM settings required to integrate with QM. In the
next section, we’ll discuss the QM master data setup required in embedded EWM. It’s
also important to note here that QM master data creation in SAP S/4HANA, such as
inspection characteristics, sampling procedure, inspection plan, and so on, is also
required. As QM master data in SAP S/4HANA is already discussed in sufficient detail in
Chapter 2, we’ll focus only on the QM master data part of embedded EWM.
8.2 Master Data Setup
The inspection rule is the only QM-specific master data that needs to be set up in
embedded EWM. Based on selection criteria, also known as properties, the inspection
rule determines which objects to trigger an inspection for and specifies the inspection
details—for example, the inspection process, the procedure, the inspection frequency,
and usage decision codes.
To create an inspection rule, use Transaction /SCWM/QRSETUP or follow menu path
Logistics  SCM Extended Warehouse Management  Extended Warehouse Manage-
ment  Master Data  Quality Management  Maintain Inspection Rule (see Figure 8.12).
Figure 8.12 Maintaining Inspection Rule

8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management
374
Tips and Tricks
The system won’t recognize the embedded EWM transaction (Transaction /SCWM/
QRSETUP) you’ve just entered in the command bar. Therefore, every embedded EWM
transaction is to be preceded by /n followed by the embedded EWM transaction. For
this example, enter the transaction as “/n/SCWM/QRSETUP” in the command bar
instead of “/SCWM/QRSETUP”.
The rest of this chapter will discuss the embedded EWM transactions without repeat-
edly mentioning to add “/n”.
To create a new inspection rule, choose Create. In this example, we’re creating an
inspection rule for IOT 4 Q – Inspection Inbound Delivery for embedded EWM product
RM124. If an inspection rule is already created and changes are required, then select
the second line item, and choose the Change (pen) icon to open the screen shown in
Figure 8.13.
In the Inspection Process field in the Properties area, enter “0”. In the Product field,
enter “RM124”. This indicates that whenever an inbound delivery item contains prod-
uct RM124, the inspection rule triggers the creation of an inspection document for the
delivery item of product RM124. Scroll down so that the screen in Figure 8.14 appears.
Figure 8.13 Inspection Rule (1/2)

8.2 Master Data Setup
Note
To configure the quality inspection group in an inspection rule so you can assign it in
the screen in Figure 8.13, follow menu path SAP IMG  SCM Extended Warehouse
Management  Extended Warehouse Management  Cross Process Settings  Quality
Management  Settings for Inspection Rules  Maintain Inspection Rule Group.
In the screen in Figure 8.14, in the Arguments - Inspection Type Detailed Data area, the
settings are almost all the same for an inspection type and are extensively discussed in
Chapter 2. In the Task List Type field, enter “Q” (Inspection Plan), followed by entering the
previously created inspection plan Group as “6” and its associated Group Counter as “1”.
Figure 8.14 Inspection Rule (2/2)
Note
If you leave the Task List Group and Group Counter fields shown in Figure 8.14 empty,
then SAP S/4HANA determines the inspection plan automatically. If you specify the
task list group and the group counter, then SAP S/4HANA doesn’t determine the
inspection plan. Instead, the inspection plan is determined based on the embedded
EWM inspection rule settings.
In the following sections, we’ll show an end-to-end business process of embedded
EWM and QM integration that uses the previously configured objects, as well as QM
master data setup for both embedded EWM and SAP S/4HANA.

8 Integrating with Embedded Extended Warehouse Management
376
8.3 Business Processes
With the necessary and QM-specific configuration and master data already set up, let’s
now discuss the business processes. Starting from the top-left side, Figure 8.15 shows an
end-to-end process flow wherein a purchase order for a supplier is created while ensur-
ing that confirmation control (inbound delivery) is in place. Next, an inbound delivery
in SAP S/4HANA is created with reference to the purchase order and the supplier. On
saving the inbound delivery document, the data automatically gets transferred or dis-
tributed to the warehouse management system (WMS). This automatic distribution of
data creates a corresponding but completely interlinked inbound delivery document
in embedded EWM. Embedded EWM processes such as unloading and goods receipt are
performed. On goods receipt in embedded EWM, the system automatically creates a
QM inspection lot, for which results are recorded and a usage decision is made. The
stock is put away and the inventory figures updated in not just the inventory manage-
ment area of SAP S/4HANA but also in embedded EWM.
Figure 8.15 Quality Management Integration with Embedded EWM
Next, let’s show the integration business process in SAP S/4HANA and in embedded
EWM.
8.3.1 Create Purchase Order with Inbound Delivery
Figure 8.16 is the display purchase order for the NB Standard PO 4500001852. The pur-
chase order was created using Transaction ME21N, followed by entering Supplier
“EWM17-SU01”, Material “RM124”, Quantity of “10” PC, Net Price of “100” USD per PC,
and Plant “1710”. In the Confirmations tab located on the lower half of the screen,
choose 0004 Inbound Delivery from the dropdown, and save the purchase order. If a
purchase order is subject to an approval or a release, then use Transaction ME29N to
release it.

8.3.2 Create Inbound Delivery in SAP S/4HANA
Figure 8.17 shows inbound delivery 180000052 for purchase order 4500001852. The
inbound delivery was created using Transaction VL31N. On the initial screen that
appears, enter Supplier “EWM17-SU01” and the Purchase Order “4500001852”, and press
(Enter). In the detailed inbound delivery screen that you see in Figure 8.17, all informa-
tion will automatically appear from the purchase order, so no data entry is required.
Figure 8.17 Inbound Delivery
Save the inbound delivery, and a message will appear informing you that it’s distrib-
uted to a WMS, which means no further direct changes to the inbound delivery can be

made (via Transaction VL32N). You can, however, display the inbound delivery in SAP
S/4HANA via Transaction VL33N.
8.3.3 Create Inbound Delivery and Goods Receipt in Embedded Extended
Warehouse Management
Access the screen shown in Figure 8.18, which is the inbound delivery maintenance in
embedded EWM, via Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. From the top dropdown, choose Pur-
chase Order, followed by entering the purchase order created in SAP S/4HANA, which is
“4500001852”, and click Search/Execute. To search via the inbound delivery created in
SAP S/4HANA, choose Logistics Execution Delivery followed by entering the inbound
delivery number (in this example, “180000052”). The embedded EWM inbound deliv-
ery document was immediately and automatically created when the SAP S/4HANA
inbound delivery was created and distributed to embedded EWM. The lower half of the
screen references the SAP S/4HANA inbound delivery document 180000052. Check
out the other tabs located at the bottom of the screen and the various icons to learn
more.
Figure 8.18 Inbound Delivery in Embedded EWM
Select the embedded EWM inbound delivery document 26 shown in Figure 8.19, click
the Unload button, and then click Goods Receipt + Save. Doing so will automatically
and immediately create the QM inspection lot shown in Figure 8.20 in the next section.
There’s also another way to receive goods in embedded EWM via Transaction /SCWM/
GR. Here, enter the purchase order, select the checkbox under the GR column, and
finally click Post Goods Receipt located on the right side of the screen.

S/4HANA, which is now assigned to this inspection lot so that the system is able to
calculate the sample size, which can be checked in the Inspection Lot Quantities

Figure 8.24 shows the detailed screen to record a decision for inspection lot
170000000653. Click the Inspection Can be Created/Changed icon under the Action
column, and the detailed screen shown in the lower half will appear. Here, choose usage

8.3.5 Display Quality Inspection Details
The screen in Figure 8.25 is accessed via Transaction /SCWM/PRDI. Select the line item
in the lower half of the screen, and click the Display Additional Data icon (hidden
behind the Display Elements option) so that options to display various elements are
shown, including Display Quality Inspection (Item). Clicking it will display the associ-
ated QM inspection lot, which in this example is 170000000653.

Some of the key features of this app include the following:

8.5 Summary
This chapter started by covering the QM-specific configuration needed to integrate with
embedded EWM in SAP S/4HANA. Next, the embedded EWM-specific QM master data
setup was discussed, followed by the end-to-end business processes in SAP S/4HANA.
The chapter also presented the warehouse monitor—a powerful tool that offers detailed
information and insights into warehouse operation using embedded EWM.
The next chapter discusses batch management.
